comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
`ControlPersist=no` is confirmed as both the fix and the workaround. Running the same `master_arguments` command with the option added, against the same host:

    spawned pid 70064 STILL ALIVE after 5s
    pgrep -f probe2.ctl -> 70064          <- one master, and it is the process that was spawned
    HERDR_SOCKET_PATH=/tmp/probe2.sock herdr workspace list -> answers

So the option keeps ssh in the foreground without costing the forward, and `child.try_wait()` then answers the question `supervise` is asking. The same command without it exits within four seconds and hands the forward to a different pid.

Until the fix lands, a user hits this only if their ssh config sets `ControlPersist` for the host, and they can neutralize it per daemon without touching `~/.ssh/config`:

    [[daemon]]
    id = "devenv"
    host = "aterp-chco"
    ssh_options = ["-o", "ControlPersist=no"]

`master_arguments` appends `forward.options` after Muster's own, and a command-line `-o` beats the config file, so this reaches ssh as the effective value. That it works from `ssh_options` at all is the argument for pinning it in `master_arguments` instead: the workaround proves the option belongs with the other four Muster already refuses to let a config override.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Verified in the real app, not just by hand. Applied `ssh_options = ["-o", "ControlPersist=no"]` to the devenv `[[daemon]]` block and relaunched (run 73812):

    tunnel events for the whole run:  1  (tunnel.open, nothing else)
    ssh masters:                      1, PPID 73812
    problems raised:                  0

Two numbers say it worked. The master's parent is the app, so it stayed in the foreground and `try_wait` is now asking about the connection itself. And the run has no `tunnel.down` at all, where every previous launch opened with two `down` / `reopened` pairs in its first three seconds. Those startup pairs were never "the normal blip" the card `a_2IRdZK6Un` describes; they were this bug, small.

All seven panes came back. Two had their attach refused by far-side clients left over from the flapping run, and Muster retried with `takeover=true` 200ms later and both became typeable, so the `a_2HrmSyRAQ` recovery path works once the tunnel underneath it holds still.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Plugging a laptop back in still leaves every devenv pane dead, on 0.5.0, over a tunnel that works. `a_2IRdZK6Un` fixed the backoff and the false `tunnel.reopened` lines; the flap itself survived, at 31 seconds instead of 1.26. This card is the cause that card could not find, and it is now measured rather than guessed: `ControlPersist` in the user's ssh config makes the master fork into the background, so `supervise` watches a process that has already exited and calls a healthy connection down forever.

## What was measured

Run 2227, 0.5.0, after unplugging ethernet and plugging it back in:

    31 tunnel.down / 25 tunnel.reopened / 5 tunnel.reopen_failed over 775 seconds, still going when the log was read
    gap from a confirmed tunnel.reopened to the next tunnel.down: min 0.251s, median 0.254s, max 0.283s

A quarter of a second is `POLL` (`crates/muster-ssh/src/tunnel.rs:344`). So the first poll after every confirmed reopen declares the connection down, 25 times out of 25.

The connection was working throughout. Asked directly, through the same forwarded socket the app was calling down:

    HERDR_SOCKET_PATH=/private/tmp/muster-2227-devenv.sock herdr workspace list
    -> workspace w4 "chicago", 7 panes, 2 tabs, agent_status "working"

Seventeen minutes of `tunnel.down` about a socket that answers on the first ask.

## The cause

`~/.ssh/config` sets `ControlPersist 10m` for this host. With `ControlPersist`, `ssh -N -M` forks into the background once it has authenticated: the process Muster spawned exits and a different pid holds the forward.

Run the exact `master_arguments` command by hand and watch it happen:

    ssh -N -M -S /tmp/probe.ctl -L /tmp/probe.sock:<remote> -o BatchMode=yes \
        -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes -o ServerAliveInterval=15 -o ServerAliveCountMax=3 <host> &
    spawned pid=49746
    (4s later) spawned pid EXITED
    pgrep -f probe.ctl -> 49757        <- a different process holds the forward
    HERDR_SOCKET_PATH=/tmp/probe.sock herdr workspace list -> answers

So the two health checks in `supervise` disagree because they are asking about different things. `confirm` asks the transport - is the socket bound, does a command come back over the master - and is right. `child.try_wait()` asks about a pid that handed off 250ms ago and is wrong. The loop believes the second.

What follows is worse than a wrong log line. On each false `tunnel.down` the loop unlinks `local_socket` and `control_path` before respawning, out from under a master that is alive and carrying traffic. Every bridge rides that `-S` path, which is why all six panes died with `herdr's stream ended without a closing frame` within five seconds of the first false down, and why the three replacements spawned with `--takeover` died the same way ninety seconds later. The respawn policy then hit `LIMIT` and stopped, correctly: from its side three bridges had failed in half a minute.

`master_arguments` pins `BatchMode`, `ExitOnForwardFailure`, `ServerAliveInterval` and `ServerAliveCountMax`, and its comment says Muster's options "are not overridable... what make a broken tunnel fail loudly instead of hanging a window". `ControlPersist` decides whether the child being supervised is the connection at all, and it is left to whatever the user's config says.

## Why the suite missed it

`a_2IRdZK6Un` was validated against the devenv container, and `a_master_that_was_killed_comes_back_still_carrying_commands` runs under `./dev --ssh`. A container's ssh config has no `ControlPersist`, so the spawned child is the master there and `try_wait` means what `supervise` assumes. The bug needs a client config that sets it, which is a common thing for a person to have and impossible for the container to have by accident.

## Fix

Add `-o ControlPersist=no` to `master_arguments`, beside the four options already pinned there for the same reason. The spawned child is then the master, and `try_wait` answers the question `supervise` is actually asking.

Worth deciding alongside it: whether `supervise` should trust the transport over the pid at all. `confirm` already knows how to ask "is this connection carrying commands", and a supervisor that polled that instead of process liveness would be right regardless of what any future ssh option does about forking. Pinning the option is the small fix; this is the one that stops the class.

## One thing not established

The tunnel was quiet for five hours between launch and the replug, so the fork is not fatal every time. At launch two `tunnel.down` / `tunnel.reopened` pairs fired in the first three seconds and then nothing until 13:45. Of the three masters alive for pid 2227 at that point, two had been reparented to init and one still had `PPID 2227` - a child that did not background. After the replug every master has `PPID 1`. What makes ssh keep the master in the foreground on some spawns is not known, and it is worth knowing before fixing, because it decides whether `ControlPersist=no` is the whole answer or only removes the common case.

## Reproducing it

1. Set `ControlPersist` for the devenv host in `~/.ssh/config`.
2. Open remote panes and let them render.
3. Unplug the network, wait about a minute, plug back in.
4. Watch `~/Library/Logs/muster/latest.jsonl`. `tunnel.reopened` and `tunnel.down` alternate about every 31 seconds and never settle, each reopen confirming the socket is bound.
5. Ask the forwarded socket directly with `herdr workspace list` while the log says the tunnel is down. It answers.

## Validating a fix

- After the network returns, the tunnel settles and `tunnel.settled` is logged once.
- A confirmed `tunnel.reopened` is not followed by a `tunnel.down` 250ms later.
- Bridges survive a replug, or are replaced within the respawn limit and stay.
- `pgrep -f 'ssh -N -M -S .*muster'` shows one master per remote daemon, not one per reopen (`a_2J1KYPWhZ`).
- The negative case still holds: a host that is genuinely unreachable backs off and reports it.
title: 🔁 ControlPersist makes ssh fork, so the tunnel supervisor watches a process that already exited
